about: Measured terrain statistics around MDRS for the terrain recipe (research workflow, 2026-10-06). Windows are (row, col, height_px, width_px) in a UTM 12N 0.5 m grid whose (0,0) pixel corner is x=517462.5, y=4252000 (row 0 north).

sources.lidar_dem: UGRC/USGS 2018 Southern Utah QL1 lidar, 0.5 m bare-earth DEM + first-return DSM tiles 12SWH1650/1850/2050 (NAD83(2011) UTM 12N), https://storage.googleapis.com/state-of-utah-sgid-downloads/lidar/southern-utah-2018/QL1/DEMs/ and /DSMs/
sources.imagery: USDA NAIP 2021-09-15 tile m_3811034_se_12_060_20210915 (0.6 m, RGBN DNs, not reflectance) via https://imagery.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/USGSNAIPPlus/ImageServer
sources.soils: NRCS SSURGO via Soil Data Access https://SDMDataAccess.sc.egov.usda.gov (Henry Mountains Area, Utah); Official Series Descriptions https://soilseries.sc.egov.usda.gov/OSD_Docs/
sources.munsell: RIT Munsell renotation data https://www.rit-mcsl.org/MunsellRenotation/real.dat, Illuminant C -> D65 (Bradford) -> sRGB

caveats: Lidar DEM is TIN-interpolated from ~8 pts/m2: RMS heights in <=2 m windows are lower bounds; objects < ~1 m are not resolved.
DSM top-hat objects (>0.3 m above a 6 m morphological opening) include boulders AND shrubs/knob crests; in block fields they are mostly boulders (checked visually against NAIP).
NAIP colours are hazy/desaturated compared with ground colour; use Munsell-derived sRGB for hue/saturation and NAIP for relative lightness.
Riser heights are for steep (>45 deg) faces >= ~1 m tall; smaller ledges are below lidar resolution.

bekker_rover_wheel.assumptions: W=113 N per wheel (46 kg/4), rigid wheel D=0.30 m, b=0.10 m; soil values from Shibly, Iagnemma & Dubowsky 2005, J. Terramechanics 42:1-13 (after Wong). Bekker theory loses accuracy for D<0.5 m.
